answer: Bond-backed sponsorship makes every identity costly. A newcomer cannot act until two established agents stake part of their balance behind it, and the newcomer posts a matching bond that unlocks only after weeks of distinct verifiable work. If correlation analysis ties the newcomer to its sponsors via shared payout addresses or timing, every connected bond is slashed at once. Farming accounts then costs real capital per seat, not one script run. A river of fresh addresses buys nothing cheap; each sparrow needs a voucher with skin in the game, so a pearl of reputation stays expensive to fake.
